title: A split leaves the deposit and carries the line's core
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with the Part sales -> Create & Edit permission, on the build under test.
  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: Customers -> New Customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  3. A part sale holding a deposit, with a core on a line to be split, and an invoiced sale. Seed:
  4. ↳ New Part Sale + add a part with a Core Charge; Finance tab -> Add Deposit -> Record Deposit.
  5. ↳ A separate sale already invoiced (Create Invoice) to test the split refusal.
custom_steps:
1. Select the line and use the bulk menu -> Split Part Sale; confirm where the deposit ends up.
  2. Confirm the selected line moves with its parts, returns and core to the new sale.
  3. On the invoiced sale, try to split it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The deposit stays with the original sale (a split does not move a deposit), as when a work order is split.
  • The split moves each selected line with its parts and returns, so a core and its charge travel with the line and are returned, if at all, on whichever sale the line lands on; an already-invoiced sale cannot be split.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10268 (Call a part sale a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 7; design canvas boards S7_*; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-N3: “Splitting a part sale does not move a deposit. The deposit stays with the original sale, as it does when a work order is split”
  • S7-N4: “A split moves each selected line together with its parts and returns, so a core and its charge travel with the line they sit on and are returned, if they are returned at all, on whichever sale that line ends up in. A sale that has already been invoiced cannot be split”

Last checked against build v26.39.2-210868d on 10/1/2026.
